substantive_reconstruction.stages_and_basis: On C×(S×H), selectorLift(P)=I_C⊗(P⊗I_H): |c,s,x>→sum_t P[t,s]|c,t,x>. AmplitudeLift sends |c,s,x>→sum_d R_(s,x)[d,c]|d,s,x>, preserving control LABELS but potentially entangling registers. SELECT sends |c,s,x>→|c,s,p_s(x)>. W's rightmost factor acts first: P, then amplitude, then SELECT, then P† on the same selector. No chronology reversal or claim of unchanged reduced controls is made.
substantive_reconstruction.clean_entry_derivation: For clean labels c0,s0 and v_s=P[s,s0], the first three stages on J|y> give sum_(s,c)v_s R_(s,y)[c,c0]|c,s,p_s(y)>. Final clean selector bra is(P†)[s0,s]=conj(v_s). Hence K[x,y]=sum_s1[p_s(y)=x]conj(v_s)R_(s,y)[c0,c0]v_s. The coefficient block is indexed by original y, not p_s(y), because amplitude occurs BEFORE SELECT. P unitary gives sum|v_s|²=1, but numerical/complex LCU weights also depend on the chosen entries, not on unitarity alone.
substantive_reconstruction.nonunique_final: For nonidentity unitary D fixing the clean BRA, <s0|D=<s0|, put Q=DP†. Q≠P† by invertibility of P, Q is unitary and its clean row equals P†'s. Lifted W_Q=D_lift W and J†D_lift=J†, so EVERY clean block entry is identical. With a qubit selector, s0=0,D=diag(1,-1) is explicit. P=A=S=I gives distinct full W=I,W_Q=D_lift with identical K=I. This is not merely accidental equality of one test vector.
substantive_reconstruction.full_inverse_boundary: If instead QP=I on the ENTIRE selector, multiplication on the right by P† yields Q=P†. That stronger full inverse task does have uniqueness. Equality of a clean projected row/block is weaker; a gate can differ on the orthogonal selector sector. A known different gate need not work, but failure of arbitrary alternatives to be guaranteed is not proof of uniqueness of all suitable alternatives.
substantive_reconstruction.explicit_selector_leakage: With singleton coefficient, selector/system qubits, P=H, amplitudeI,SELECT controlled(I,X), the clean input|0,0> becomes Bell(|00>+|11>)/sqrt2 before finalH. Afterwards it is(|00>+|10>+|01>-|11>)/2. Selector1 has norm²1/2, so deterministic cleanup fails despite all source hypotheses. K=(I+X)/2; K|0>=(|0>+|1>)/2 has norm²1/2 and its conditioned normalized state is|+>. The full state includes a nonzero rejected sector. For input|->, K annihilates it, so no normalized accepted state exists; no general no-kernel assumption was inserted.
substantive_reconstruction.coefficient_cleanup_and_domains: The accepted injection fixes BOTH coefficient and selector, not the system. Coefficient leakage is likewise possible: e.g. selector/system singleton, amplitude coefficient X and clean coefficient0 give output coefficient1 under the chosen architecture. In general deterministic cleanup would require(I-JJ†)WJ=0. Clean labels require actual nonempty auxiliary carriers; abstract unitary identities can be vacuous on empty finite spaces, but examples instantiate explicit nonempty qubits/singletons.
